name: Reply to new real estate leads in minutes with Claude, Follow Up Boss and Twilio

parameters.content:
## Reply to new real estate leads in minutes with Claude, Follow Up Boss and Twilio

Real-estate agents and teams who lose portal leads to whoever answers first.

### How it works
Trigger: A lead email from Zillow or Realtor.com, a website form submission, or a new person appearing in Follow Up Boss or kvCORE starts the run.
1. Receive the lead
2. Look up the lead in the CRM
3. Qualify
4. Draft the first reply
5. Check quiet hours and consent
6. Send the reply
7. Log and hand off
8. Follow up on silence
Every AI step is followed by a "Needs a person?" gate that parks low-confidence items.

### Setup
1. Open "Config (edit me)" and fill in the fields (names, approver, quiet hours, thresholds).
2. Add credentials: Anthropic, plus Follow Up Boss / kvCORE / HubSpot, Gmail / Outlook, Twilio.
3. Run once with test_mode on, read the output, then switch the trigger on.

### Customization tips
Put your first-reply rules and quiet hours in the Config node; swap Follow Up Boss for kvCORE or HubSpot and Twilio for your SMS provider.
Guardrail to keep: Quiet hours: nothing sent 9 pm–8 am in the lead's time zone; messages queue until morning.

Full blueprint: https://agentmelt.com/workflows/speed-to-lead-automation/

## 1. Receive the lead
Name, email, phone, source, the property or page they enquired from, and their message

nodes.name: Section: 2. Look up the lead in the CRM

parameters.content:
## 2. Look up the lead in the CRM
Existing record, past conversations, stage, and any notes — so the reply does not treat a past client like a stranger

## 3. Qualify
Timeline, pre-approval, price band and intent from the enquiry text; 'hot' only when the timeline is near and something specific is named

## 4. Draft the first reply
Two to four sentences in the agent's voice, referencing the property or page, with exactly one question

nodes.name: Section: 5. Check quiet hours and consent

parameters.content:
## 5. Check quiet hours and consent
Holds the message until quiet hours end in the lead's time zone; checks that a phone number came with consent before any SMS; skips leads who opted out

## 6. Send the reply
From the agent's own address, threaded to the lead's email where there is one; SMS as an optional second channel

## 7. Log and hand off
Note and stage written to the CRM; hot leads text the agent a three-line summary with the number to call

## 8. Follow up on silence
Two days without a reply: one nudge that offers two showing slots or asks what they are after

## Fill this in first
Every later node reads these values. Keep test_mode on for the first week.

nodes.name: Config (edit me)
nodes.notes:
Fill these in once; every later node reads them as $('Config (edit me)').item.json.config.*

test_mode = true: log what the workflow would write, without writing it, for the first week.
approval_mode = true: the approval node waits for a person; switch off per message type once it has earned it.

Also point the nodes at your own sources:
- Portal lead emails or site form
- CRM (Follow Up Boss, kvCORE, HubSpot)
- Agent voice samples
- Calendar for showing slots
- Consent and opt-out records

options.systemMessage:
You are the "Qualify" step of the Speed-to-Lead Automation Workflow workflow run by Agentmelt.
Task: Timeline, pre-approval, price band and intent from the enquiry text; 'hot' only when the timeline is near and something specific is named. Nothing is inferred beyond the text.

Rules:
- Quiet hours: nothing sent 9 pm–8 am in the lead's time zone; messages queue until morning.
- One question per message; the second message asks the next question, never both at once.
- SMS only with a number the lead gave on a form; STOP honoured on the first word and written to the CRM.
- Fair-housing language check on every draft; flagged drafts cannot be sent.
- Approval mode for the first week: drafts go to the agent for a tap before sending.
- Answer only from the data provided in the input. If something is missing, say so in the output instead of guessing.
- If this step produces a message or a document, put the full text in `draft` (and a `subject` if it is an email); put a one-line summary in `summary`.
- Set `needs_human` true whenever you are unsure, the input is unusual, or a rule above applies; a person will look at it.
- Return valid JSON matching the output schema; no prose outside the JSON.

nodes.name: Needs a person?
nodes.notes: True = the AI step was not sure or flagged the item → dead letter, a person looks. False = continue. Wire the dead letter to a Slack message or a sheet so nothing fails silently.

nodes.name: Needs a person: Qualify
nodes.notes: Dead letter. Replace this no-op with a Slack message or a sheet row that carries the raw item and the reason — silent failures are the ones that cost.

Two to four sentences in the agent's voice, referencing the property or page, with exactly one question. Fair-housing wordlist applied.
